title: Reproducing the article
text: 01_data.R calls download_physionet() MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, MIT-BIH Supraventricular Arrhythmia Database St Petersburg INCART database, read_database() segment first signal (lead II INCART) windows 61, 31 43 samples around annotated R peaks. also downloads 49 industry portfolios French data library standardizes within year. 02_heldout.R leaves one record time, one patient INCART, estimates every operator others: pool_spectral(), pool_covariance(), pool_bases(), hierarchical_pool(), energy_moment() pool_shared(), dct_basis(). records mean per-beat error, ratio traces, rate rate_distortion() separation normal ventricular beats. 03_summary.R computes paired bootstrap intervals records patients writes tables values.tex. 04_figures.R draws figures. scripts live system.file("article", package = "beatpool").

title: Moment Pooling of PCA Bases for ECG Heartbeat Compression
text: Moment pooling PCA bases ECG heartbeats beatpool represents heartbeats patient-specific principal component bases, pools bases across sites without sharing raw signals, provides reconstruction, clustering stability tools used accompanying study. pure-R reader WFDB headers, signals annotations included, full pipeline runs without external WFDB software.

title: Moment Pooling of PCA Bases for ECG Heartbeat Compression
text: recording covariance structure, basis fitted one patient directly comparable basis fitted another. Pooling bases entry entry fails principal components defined signs, permutations rotations. beatpool offers two families solutions: Alignment-based pooling removes indeterminacy orthogonal Procrustes rotation averages, takes orthogonal Procrustes mean (default), column-normalised mean QR retraction. Moment pooling never aligns anything. site sends leading eigenpairs \((Q_h, \lambda_h)\) server assembles \(\hat\Sigma = \sum_h w_h Q_h \Lambda_h Q_h'\). outer product invariant orthogonal transformation \(Q_h\), leading eigenvectors \(\hat\Sigma\) Eckart-Young optimal pooled second moment.

code: library(beatpool)  sim <- simulate_beats(H = 8, n = 200, p = 61, q = 10,                       model = "heterogeneous", epsilon = 0.2, seed = 1) bases <- extract_bases(sim$X, q = 10)  pooled <- pool_bases(bases, method = "procrustes")   # aligned mean spec   <- pool_spectral(bases, q = 10)               # moment pooling  reconstruction_error(sim$X[[1]], pooled$T, k = 10) reconstruction_error(sim$X[[1]], spec$T, k = 10)  # every operator in the paper, with its communication cost all <- pool_all(sim$X, q = 10) attr(all, "numbers") x <- read_wfdb("100", dir = "data/mitdb") ann <- read_annotations("data/mitdb/atr/100.atr") X <- prepare_record(x$MLII, ann, record = "100", fs = 360, wsize = 30) b <- pca_basis(X, q = 10)

title: Attention weights over transmitted moments — attention_weights
text: Scores transmitted moment query moment turns scores weights. key record \(h\) projector \(P_h\) onto leading k eigenvectors. score = "energy" score \(s_h = tr(P_h R_0)\), \(R_0\) energy-normalised moment query; \(R_0\) full moment set beats, \(1 - s_h\) mean per-beat relative error basis record \(h\). score = "projection" score \(tr(P_h P_0)/k\), symmetric two subspaces, \(P_0\) projects onto leading k eigenvectors \(R_0\). score = "cosine" cosine \(R_0\) \(M_h\) Frobenius inner product. scores depend eigenvectors \(P_h\) \(M_h\), therefore unchanged signs, order rotation within retained subspace.
